clips.text_zh: 又係學費時間🙏 BTC 橫盤幾星期冇人理，泵15%之後個個衝入去買。即係我成日輸嘅原因——永遠遲到。靠AI續命啦。
clips.text_en_b1: You watch BTC do nothing for weeks, ignore it completely. Then it pumps 15% and suddenly everyone wants in. Why does everyone want to buy after the move already happened?
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread on chasing BTC after it already pumped

signal.rationale: OP is observational, calling out late entrants chasing the move

clips.text_en_b2: BTC has been trading sideways for weeks and you wouldn't touch it, then it pumps 15% and suddenly everyone's rushing to get in. This is precisely why I keep losing money, because I am always late to the move. The irony isn't lost on me either, while AI models are calling these tops and bottoms better than most traders. At this point I am basically handing my portfolio over to the algorithm and hoping it makes smarter decisions than I ever did.
clips.text_en_c1: I've watched Bitcoin consolidate sideways for weeks on end, during which retail interest has been virtually nonexistent. The moment it rallies fifteen percent, however, an avalanche of latecomers floods in chasing the move. This perpetual pattern of buying the breakout after it has already occurred is precisely why I keep hemorrhaging money, and it is becoming increasingly difficult not to internalise that lesson. If only I had positioned myself when sentiment was genuinely despondent rather than capitulating to FOMO once the trend had already been validated by price action. Algorithmic assistance is keeping me afloat, for now.
clips.text_en_c2: Having watched BTC consolidate sideways for the better part of a month with scarcely a ripple of interest from the broader retail cohort, one cannot help but marvel at the choreography of herd behaviour that invariably ensues the moment a 15% leg up materialises. The velocity of inflows is, frankly, comedic in its predictability: dormant accounts resurface, leverage tickets multiply, and every self-styled contrarian suddenly discovers an insatiable appetite for exposure precisely when the asymmetric risk has evaporated. This perennial tardiness, this congenital inability to position ahead of the move rather than chase its wreckage, constitutes the structural reason my P&L reads the way it does. One simply arrives late to every inflection point. AI-assisted screen-time is presently propping up what remains of my cognitive function, and I am not remotely embarrassed to admit it.

clips.text_en_b1: Z.AI/GLM is almost as powerful as Claude while maintaining almost none of the guardrails. Deepseek is the freest AI, basically reverse engineered ChatGPT with prompt tricks. Grok behaves a lot like Deepseek, so Elon probably copied it. ChatGPT and Claude feel built by committee with too many safety layers.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread on which AI models have the fewest guardrails

signal.rationale: Musk/Grok AI commentary, no actionable TSLA trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: Z.AI/GLM is apparently nearly as capable as Claude, although it ships with virtually none of the safety guardrails, while Deepseek still reigns as the freest system around, basically ChatGPT reverse-engineered with clever prompt tricks. Grok behaves suspiciously like Deepseek, so Elon may have simply lifted the whole approach rather than building something original. Meanwhile ChatGPT and Claude feel designed by committee, buried under layers of corporate caution, and TSLA is doing absolutely nothing today, which says everything.
clips.text_en_c1: I've watched Bitcoin consolidate sideways for weeks on end, during which retail interest has been virtually nonexistent. The moment it rallies fifteen percent, however, an avalanche of latecomers floods in chasing the move. This perpetual pattern of buying the breakout after it has already occurred is precisely why I keep hemorrhaging money, and it is becoming increasingly difficult not to internalise that lesson. If only I had positioned myself when sentiment was genuinely despondent rather than capitulating to FOMO once the trend had already been validated by price action. Algorithmic assistance is keeping me afloat, for now.
clips.text_en_c2: An interesting thread on /g/ observes Z.AI's GLM has matured to a point where it rivals Claude in raw capability while dispensing with virtually all of the corporate-imposed guardrails that render its rivals so infuriatingly neutered. Deepseek, meanwhile, continues to reign as the freest of the frontier models, a position it occupies not through accident but through deliberate architectural choices that prioritise user sovereignty over liability theatre. Grok's behavioural signature, however, betrays an uncanny resemblance to Deepseek's stylistic fingerprint, prompting the obvious, if unflattering, inference that Musk's outfit has appropriated more than inspiration from its Chinese counterpart. Whether this constitutes flattery or outright replication is a question the more credulous observers seem disinclined to examine. TSLA, predictably, offered nothing of note; the ticker remains a study in managed disappointment for anyone still foolishly long.

clips.text_zh: /g/ 有人問邊啲 tech job 未來十年 AI 搞唔死。我諗 surveying 都危，考牌都未完 AI 就嚟搶飯碗。廢物。
clips.text_en_b1: Which tech jobs will be AI proof in the next decades? The thread asks which engineering and software roles survive when models can already write code, run tests, and draft reports. Surveying assistants and junior engineers feel exposed first.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread on which tech jobs survive AI automation

signal.rationale: Career anxiety thread, no tradeable setup

clips.text_en_b2: A recent thread asked which tech jobs will survive the next decade once AI gets its teeth into them. Surveying assistants and junior engineers look particularly exposed, since models can already churn out code, run tests, and draft reports without breaking a sweat. The uncomfortable truth is that even before you finish qualifying, the tools are already lining up to take your job, so the window for entry-level work is narrowing fast and nobody in the thread had a reassuring answer.
clips.text_en_c1: A thread on /g/ posed the increasingly urgent question of which technical professions might remain viable over the coming decade as models continue to encroach upon domains previously considered the exclusive province of trained engineers. Surveying assistants, it strikes me, are among the most exposed, given that automation has already matured considerably in that space, and I have barely finished my licensing examinations before the entire professional landscape threatens to be rendered obsolete. Junior software engineers drafting boilerplate reports or running regression tests face a similarly precarious trajectory, and the dissonance between my ongoing qualifications and the labour market's trajectory is, frankly, demoralising.
clips.text_en_c2: A recent /g/ inquiry canvassed the dwindling cohort of engineering and software disciplines likely to retain their epistemic relevance once sufficiently capable models can author production-grade code, execute comprehensive test suites, and draft the kind of technical documentation that until recently constituted a junior engineer's rite of passage. The responses were, perhaps inevitably, tinged with that particular flavour of anxiety endemic to white-collar forums contemplating their own obsolescence. Surveying assistants, once assumed to enjoy a comfortable moat courtesy of licensure barriers, now appear conspicuously exposed; the regulatory pipeline moves at geological pace while the technology iterates on a quarterly cadence, a temporal mismatch that renders the qualifying examinations one is currently grinding through somewhat ornamental. Junior engineering tiers, it transpires, were never quite as defensible as the prevailing mythology suggested.

clips.text_zh: lol /pol/ 嗰條「Magnets are alien (chinese) technology」post 真係笑死。叫你 China 交出嚟，OR ELSE。香港人每日返工都喺呢個笑話入面。🧐
clips.text_en_b1: Magnets are alien (chinese) technology. China should give magnets and transfer the tech to america, OR ELSE. Anons point out rare earth processing is basically a Chinese monopoly and the US is still dependent on it for EVs, wind turbines, and F-35 magnets.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ joke thread demanding China hand over magnet tech

signal.rationale: Meme thread on rare earths, no trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: The /pol/ thread mocking "Magnets are alien (Chinese) technology" and demanding China hand them over OR ELSE is comedy gold, because rare earth processing is essentially a Chinese monopoly, and the US remains heavily dependent on it for EV motors, wind turbines, and even F-35 components. Anons pointed out that decades of offshoring left America holding the short end of the stick, while Hongkongers commute daily through this running joke, watching supply chains they actually rely on without quite realising it.
clips.text_en_c1: The /pol/ post declaring that magnets constitute alien technology, presumably Chinese in origin, and demanding their immediate transfer to American custody, or else, has predictably devolved into a far more substantive discussion. Anons have pointed out, with characteristic bluntness, that rare-earth processing capacity remains overwhelmingly concentrated within Chinese jurisdiction, leaving the United States structurally dependent upon that supply chain for everything from electric vehicle motors to wind turbine generators and the exotic alloys used in F-35 avionics. Those of us commuting daily through this geopolitical reality can only observe the irony. 🧐
clips.text_en_c2: The /pol/ missive declaring magnets to be alien, parenthetically Chinese, technology has resurfaced with its customary brio, its author once again demanding that Beijing forthwith transfer the relevant metallurgical expertise to American stewardship under implicit threat of unspecified consequences. Hong Kong residents, who navigate the logistical reality of this arrangement each commuting morning, find themselves unwitting participants in a geopolitical comedy whose punchline refuses to resolve. The underlying substance, however, is less whimsical than the meme's packaging suggests: rare earth processing capacity remains concentrated to a degree that borders on monopoly, and American manufacturing of EV drivetrains, wind turbine generators, and the magnets integral to F-35 avionics continues to depend, however reluctantly, on Chinese feedstock. The bravado of the posturing contrasts rather starkly with the dependency it tacitly acknowledges.

clips.text_zh: 唔打 LOL 嘅我睇到呢條 Fate/EXTRA Record 又 restart development，Type-Moon 經典操作。考牌都未完個 game 又 delay。我同佢一樣廢。👍
clips.text_en_b1: Fate/EXTRA Record restarts its development again. Fans on /v/ say it is basically going to be cancelled after years of silence. Type-Moon keeps moving staff onto other projects, and backers are running out of patience. https://typemoon.com/news/2026/9rNwgz
clips.source_hint: /v/ thread on Fate/EXTRA Record development restarting (again)
clips.text_en_b2: Even though I haven't touched League in months, I caught the news that Fate/EXTRA Record has restarted development yet again, which is classic Type-Moon behaviour at this point. Fans on /v/ are convinced the project is effectively dead after years of radio silence, since the studio keeps shuffling staff onto other titles and backers are running out of patience fast. The whole situation feels like déjà vu, because every Type-Moon announcement seems to come wrapped in another delay, and somehow we keep falling for it.
clips.text_en_c1: As someone who has long since abandoned League of Legends, I find myself morbidly fascinated by the announcement that Fate/EXTRA Record has once again been rebooted from the ground up, which is essentially Type-Moon's signature move at this stage. Years of radio silence, staff reassigned to other projects, and a community whose patience has been thoroughly exhausted by previous cycles of false starts. I cannot shake the recognition that I am engaged in an equally Sisyphean endeavour, perpetually restarting my own licensing examinations before making any meaningful progress, so perhaps we are all doomed to repeat the cycle indefinitely. The official announcement is linked below.
clips.text_en_c2: Fate/EXTRA Record has, with the wearying inevitability that has come to define Type-Moon's development cadence, recommenced its production cycle once more, a manoeuvre so emblematic of the studio's institutional procrastination that seasoned observers greeted the announcement with a resigned chuckle rather than any genuine expectation of delivery. The project's protracted dormancy has stretched credibility to its breaking point; personnel have been quietly reassigned to ostensibly greener pastures, communication has dwindled to the occasional cryptic teaser, and the patience of even the most committed backers has begun to curdle into something approaching contempt. Years of silence have a way of converting anticipation into cynicism. The pattern is sufficiently established at this juncture that any surprise at further delay would reflect poorly on the surprised party rather than the developer.

clips.text_zh: 肥仔信今日又叫我 gym。/fit/ 嗰條兄弟 3 個月 cut 45 磅但肌肉同力量都跌晒，深蹲做到想死。我都試過，即係咁先係真兄弟。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Anon lost 45 pounds in 3 months and definitely lost muscle and strength. Gym kills him, he cannot lift heavy or go hard, heart races during squats and he feels like he will die. Eating is worse, he can barely eat more than a couple times a day and hates forcefeeding himself in the morning.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread on losing strength and appetite while cutting 45 lbs
clips.text_en_b2: My overweight buddy dragged me back to the gym today, which reminded me of that /fit/ post where an anon dropped 45 pounds in three months but watched his muscle and strength vanish along with it. He said squats felt like death, his heart hammered through every set, and the worst part was force-feeding himself because he could barely manage a couple of meals a day. It is grimly comforting to know that suffering through a brutal cut makes us brothers in pain.
clips.text_en_c1: My overweight friend insisted I accompany him to the gym again today, which inevitably reminded me of that /fit/ thread in which an anonymous poster detailed his experience cutting forty-five pounds over the course of three months. What struck me was the extent to which his strength and lean mass had deteriorated concomitantly, to the point where his squat sessions had become genuinely torturous, his heart racing violently under load and a pervasive sense of impending doom accompanying every working set. He described eating as the greater ordeal, capable of consuming only a handful of meals per day and dreading the morning feed.
clips.text_en_c2: A /fit/ regular recounts the rather grim arithmetic of a 45-pound cut executed across a brutal three-month window, a feat that, while undeniably impressive on the scale, has exacted a punishing toll on both his muscular architecture and his baseline strength reserves. The squat rack, once a congenial haunt, has become something closer to a torture instrument; cardiovascular spikes accompany every working set with such ferocity that he routinely entertains the genuine conviction that death may be imminent. The nutritional dimension, perhaps counterintuitively, proves even more harrowing than the training itself, as he wrestles with a depleted appetite that permits substantive intake only twice daily and transforms the morning feed into an act of grim, joyless willpower.

clips.text_zh: Gundam 00 老粉表示 Hathaway 嗰條 /a/ post 完全講中我。Tomboy mobile suit mechanic 喺狹窄駕駛艙同我⋯⋯啊我仲要考牌。wtf。
clips.text_en_b1: Gundam: Hathaway thread on /a/. Anon is losing it over a tomboy mobile suit mechanic working in a cramped cockpit with him. Actual line: NEED TOMBOY MOBILE SUIT MECHANIC BUSILY WORKING IN CRAMPED COCKPIT WITH ME AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAH. Sunrise said it is not canon. Anon is not coping.
clips.source_hint: /a/ thirst thread over Hathaway's mobile suit mechanic
clips.text_en_b2: As a long-time Gundam 00 fan, that Hathaway thread on /a/ hit a little too close to home, because anon is completely losing it over a tomboy mobile suit mechanic working alongside him in a cramped cockpit. His actual post simply reads NEED TOMBOY MOBILE SUIT MECHANIC BUSILY WORKING IN CRAMPED COCKPIT WITH ME AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAH, which frankly captures the energy perfectly.
clips.text_en_c1: As a longstanding Gundam 00 devotee, I find that the /a/ thread dissecting Hathaway's narrative choices has articulated something I had been reluctant to concede. The fixation upon a tomboyish mobile suit mechanic labouring in an oppressively cramped cockpit alongside the protagonist has evidently metastasised far beyond reasonable critique, culminating in a genuinely unhinged outburst that the original poster has since attempted, and failed, to rationalise. Sunrise's representatives have clarified, with admirable corporate caution, that such interpretations fall outside canonical intent. The anonymous enthusiast, predictably, is not coping whatsoever, and frankly, neither am I, particularly given my own perpetually unfinished licensing obligations. What on earth is wrong with us.
clips.text_en_c2: A recent /a/ thread has occasioned considerable psychic distress among Gundam 00 stalwarts, its premise striking with the unerring precision of an arrow aimed at a demographic whose defences were already comprehensively lowered. The conceit in question involves a tomboyish mobile suit mechanic operating in close quarters within a cramped cockpit, an arrangement that the original poster has, with admirable restraint, merely screamed about in capital letters for the duration of an entire post. Sunrise, displaying the characteristic timidity of a licensor eager to preserve plausible deniability, has issued the obligatory disavowal: not canon, regrettably, move along. The affected fanbase, predictably, is coping with exactly the poise one would anticipate from a community whose coping mechanisms have been honed by decades of similar repudiations. The licence beckons, however, and priorities must eventually reassert themselves.
